## Where this guide fits

This guide completes the core CDI Data Science progression:

1. **Data Science Foundations** establishes reproducible analysis.
2. **Advanced Data Science** develops defensible models and analytical decisions.
3. **Model Deployment** turns a validated model into a dependable prediction service.

Deployment is treated as an extension of reproducible modelling—not as a separate collection of infrastructure tricks. The same compact classification example, feature definitions, preprocessing pipeline, and prediction contract develop across the guide.

## What you will build

By the end of the guide, you will be able to:

- train and evaluate a deployment candidate;
- save preprocessing and prediction as one scikit-learn `Pipeline`;
- load the artifact safely for batch and online inference;
- validate request data with Pydantic;
- expose predictions through FastAPI;
- test successful requests, invalid inputs, and failure conditions with `pytest`;
- package the application in a Docker image; and
- monitor input data, predictions, and operational behaviour after release.

## How the guide works

Each chapter adds one production concern without replacing the model or inventing a new example. Short code fragments in the chapters explain important ideas. Complete executable programs live under `scripts/python/`, with repeatable command-line wrappers under `scripts/bash/`.

Generated artifacts are kept in predictable locations:

| Directory | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `data/` | Raw, processed, reference, and inference data |
| `models/` | Serialized pipelines and model metadata |
| `results/` | Metrics, diagnostics, monitoring summaries, and figures |
| `reports/` | Human-readable deployment and monitoring reports |

Start with the [Preface](00-preface.qmd), then prepare the repository in [Setting Up the Environment](01-setting-up-environment.qmd).
